activities.description: Roctopus is a Dive RAID International training centre founded on Koh Tao and based in Sairee. Its current recreational model is built around small groups, with a published maximum of four divers per instructor or dive leader on its core courses and fun-diving program. The centre combines beginner training, continuing education, professional development, recreational diving and a well-documented marine-conservation program through Roctopus ecoTrust.

activities.whyChoose: It is the strongest default fit for The House guests who value instructor attention and a less anonymous training experience, particularly nervous beginners and couples.
activities.whatMakesDifferent: The combination of a published 4:1 philosophy, dedicated training facilities, RAID pathway and its own ecoTrust gives it a distinct identity among Koh Tao’s high-volume dive market.

activities.description: Sea kayaks are commonly rented from beachfront businesses and are a practical way to explore short stretches of Koh Tao’s coast when the water is calm. The experience is best treated as a near-shore activity, not an excuse for inexperienced paddlers to make exposed crossings.
activities.bestKnownFor: Independent low-cost exploration of nearby coves and coastline.
activities.whyChoose: Choose it for active couples/friends who want flexibility without booking a motorboat.
activities.whatMakesDifferent: It provides quiet, self-paced access to short coastal sections and can be combined with snorkeling from a sheltered landing point.
activities.difficulty: Easy on calm water; moderate/high in wind or swell
activities.minimumAge: Rental-provider dependent; children should paddle with an experienced adult
activities.suitableChildren: Yes only in calm water with correctly fitted PFD
activities.swimmingAbility: Basic swimming strongly recommended; PFD should be worn
activities.privateOrGroup: Self-guided rental; guided options may exist
activities.price: Hourly/half-day/day rentals are available around Koh Tao, but no island-wide 2026 tariff was independently verified
activities.equipmentIncluded: Kayak and paddle; confirm PFD is included before paying
activities.extraCosts: Dry bag, snorkel gear, deposit, taxi
activities.cancellationPolicy: Rental-provider specific; weather usually determines practical use
activities.bestMonths: Calm-water periods easiest
activities.bestTimeOfDay: Early morning is best for cooler temperatures and usually lighter wind
activities.weatherConsiderations: Do not paddle into strengthening offshore wind; conditions can change quickly around headlands
activities.crowdLevels: Low once away from main beach; boat lanes remain active
activities.whatToBring: Water, hat, reef-safe sunscreen, rash guard, dry bag, waterproof phone case, footwear that can get wet.
activities.safety: Wear a PFD. Stay close to shore and within the rental provider’s permitted zone. Do not attempt Koh Nang Yuan or long exposed crossings unless the provider confirms conditions and the paddler has genuine sea-kayak competence. Avoid ferry/longtail lanes and never tie to coral.
activities.hours: Daylight/provider-specific
activities.accessibility: Low; requires beach entry and balance
activities.mobileSignal: Generally good near Sairee; weaker around remote headlands
activities.nearby: From Sairee, combine with sunset or nearby cafés. From southern/eastern bays, remain within the sheltered bay unless local staff confirms safe coastal conditions.
activities.conciergeNotes: The common tourist mistake is paddling too far downwind and then struggling to return. Ask the renter which direction the wind is expected to build and paddle into the easier return strategy, not simply toward the prettiest headland. Early morning is materially safer and more comfortable than a windy afternoon.

activities.childFriendly: Yes with adult/PFD in calm water

activities.name: Stand-Up Paddleboarding — Sairee Sunset SUP
activities.verificationStatus: Fact-checked 7 August 2026; any unverified field is explicitly marked.
activities.description: Stand-up paddleboarding is widely available from Sairee beachfront operators and requires little formal experience in flat water. The signature Koh Tao version is a late-afternoon paddle on the west coast, staying close enough to shore to return before darkness.
activities.bestKnownFor: Easy-access sunset paddling from Koh Tao’s main west-coast beach.
activities.whyChoose: Choose it for couples, beginners and guests wanting a photogenic activity that is active without being strenuous.
activities.whatMakesDifferent: Sairee combines calm-water opportunities, rental availability and a direct west-facing sunset.
activities.minimumAge: Rental-provider dependent
activities.suitableChildren: Older children/teens can participate with supervision and PFD; younger children only with provider approval
activities.price: Hourly/half-day rental prices vary; no current universal tariff independently verified
activities.equipmentIncluded: Board and paddle; confirm leash and PFD
activities.extraCosts: Lesson, dry bag, deposit
activities.bestSeason: Year-round when west coast is calm
activities.bestMonths: Flat-water months easiest
activities.bestTimeOfDay: Late afternoon, returning before full darkness; morning is calmer for first-timers
activities.weatherConsiderations: Wind is the key limiting factor; offshore wind can carry beginners away from shore
activities.crowdLevels: Sairee busier around sunset but water space is usually manageable away from boat lanes
activities.whatToBring: Swimwear/rash guard, reef-safe sunscreen, water, waterproof phone case, hat for daytime.
activities.bookingRequired: Usually no for rental; lesson/private session should be booked
activities.advanceBooking: No for ordinary rental unless peak period
activities.safety: Use a leash/PFD as instructed. Avoid longtail and tender lanes. Do not stay offshore after dark without appropriate lights/support. Beginners should kneel until stable and remain close to shore if wind increases.
activities.hours: Daylight/provider-specific
activities.wifi: No on water; many beachfront venues
activities.nearby: Sairee restaurants, cafés and bars are immediately available after the paddle; this pairs naturally with sunset dinner.
activities.conciergeNotes: For a complete beginner, recommend a morning trial first if the afternoon forecast is breezy. For sunset, launch 45–60 minutes before sunset and stay near shore; returning in total darkness creates unnecessary boat-traffic risk. A waterproof phone lanyard is more useful than trying to balance an expensive camera loose on the board.

activities.name: John-Suwan Viewpoint
activities.area: South Koh Tao above Chalok/Freedom area
activities.verificationStatus: Fact-checked 7 August 2026; any unverified field is explicitly marked.
activities.description: John-Suwan is Koh Tao’s best-known short viewpoint hike, overlooking the southern peninsula with bays on both sides. The route is relatively short but includes steep dirt, roots and rocky scrambling near the top, so it should not be described as an effortless “five-minute photo stop.”
activities.bestKnownFor: Classic twin-bay panorama of southern Koh Tao.
activities.whyChoose: Choose it for first-time visitors wanting the strongest single viewpoint-to-effort ratio.
activities.whatMakesDifferent: Its peninsula position produces a distinctive view of water on both sides of the island.

activities.suitableChildren: Older mobile children only with close adult supervision where cliffs/rocks are present
activities.suitableBeginners: Yes for fit beginners in dry weather
activities.price: Local/private-land access fee may apply; current fee not independently verified unless stated
activities.equipmentIncluded: No technical gear for standard route; proper shoes recommended
activities.extraCosts: Access/parking fee, drinks at viewpoint businesses, taxi
activities.cancellationPolicy: Not applicable self-guided; skip in unsafe weather
activities.bestMonths: No fixed month; avoid immediately after heavy rain
activities.bestTimeOfDay: Early morning for cooler temperature and fewer people; late afternoon light can be attractive if enough daylight remains
activities.weatherConsiderations: Do not hike exposed granite in rain/thunderstorms; midday heat can be severe
activities.crowdLevels: Lowest early; highest around midday/peak arrivals
activities.whatToBring: At least 1 L water per person for longer/hot routes, closed shoes with grip, hat, sunscreen, mosquito repellent, charged phone, small cash, light snack.
activities.bookingRequired: No for normal self-guided trails unless venue requires
activities.safety: Start early enough to return before dark unless the route/venue is designed for evening access. Do not leave marked paths for cliff-edge photos. Wet granite is extremely slippery. Tell someone where you are going on remote trails and do not rely on continuous mobile signal.
activities.hours: Daylight unless venue publishes otherwise
activities.hotelPickup: Taxi can reach road approaches; final trail on foot
activities.parking: Varies; scooter access can be steep or rough
activities.drinkingWater: Bring your own even if drinks may be sold
activities.nearby: Freedom Beach, Taa Toh/Chalok and southern restaurants can be combined in the same half day.
activities.conciergeNotes: Do the hike before the beach, not after hours in the sun. Bring small cash because access fees have historically applied, but the current 2026 amount was not verified well enough to publish. Avoid after rain. At the top, wait for the main photo position rather than climbing around other people onto unstable edges.

activities.safety: Night diving requires strong buddy awareness, light signals and controlled entry/exit. Guests with poor buoyancy or high anxiety should first complete additional daytime dives. Follow the operator’s certification prerequisite and never separate from the guide/buddy.
